clue.text: Most of powerful remedy husband swallowed in style

indicators.note: something swallowed goes inside, so the husband's letter sits within the shortened remedy
most of a word means all of it bar its final letter, so the remedy loses its tail

parts.note: a panacea is a cure-all, a remedy powerful enough for every ill

explanation.surface: A strong medicine, mostly downed by a husband, taken with a certain flair.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Most of' trims PANACEA to PANACE; 'swallowed' puts H inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: Both words mean a dashing flamboyance of manner.

clue.text: Defence's loss of temper about a criminal charge

definitions.note: the definition with 's standing for is: a defence is

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the fit of temper goes round the other pieces

parts.note: a pet is a fit of sulking or temper
a rap is a criminal charge, as in a murder rap

explanation.surface: A barrister's defence fails when they lose their temper over a criminal accusation.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Defence's' reads as a legal defence in court; it is a protective wall, with 's standing for 'is'.
explanation.definitionFit: A low protective wall along a roof or rampart is a defence for those behind it.

clue.text: Refusal to corrupt early days in vocation

parts.note: no is a refusal
to vitiate is to spoil or corrupt

explanation.surface: A novice in religious life refuses to be led astray.
explanation.definitionFit: It is the probationary period served by a novice before taking religious vows.

clue.text: Simple job top commander finds hard

parts.note: C-in-C, Commander-in-Chief, is the top commander
H is the abbreviation for hard, as on pencils

explanation.surface: The general finds an easy task is actually difficult.
explanation.definitionFit: A cinch is something very easy, a sure thing.

clue.text: Candlestick finally placed in niche

indicators.note: placed in means set within, so the candle holder goes inside

parts.note: finally means in the end, giving the word end
a sconce is a wall bracket candlestick

explanation.surface: A candle holder is at last set into an alcove in the wall.
explanation.walkthrough: An &lit: read as a whole, the clue describes the answer, and 'niche' completes the picture of a wall candle holder settled snugly into an alcove.
explanation.definitionFit: To be settled snugly and securely in a spot, such as a recess, is to be comfortably tucked in.

clue.text: Slur on reputation inhibits us getting support

indicators.note: to inhibit is to hold in, so the slur holds the next word inside it

parts.note: a stain is a blot or slur on one's good name
taken as written

explanation.surface: A smear on someone's good name is keeping a group from getting backing.
explanation.definitionFit: To sustain something is to hold it up or keep it going, a synonym of support.

clue.text: Craft waiting to land a lot of wood

definitions.meaning: aircraft circling at staggered heights over an airport waiting their turn
a large pile, as of logs or timber

explanation.definitionFit: Planes held circling in layers form one; a heap of logs is another.

clue.text: One of those carrying things across a bay?

definitions.text: One of those carrying things across a bay?

parts.words: One of those carrying things across a bay?
parts.note: the bay is a reddish-brown horse, not a stretch of coast, and the thing slung across its back carries luggage

explanation.surface: A ferry or boat carrying cargo over a stretch of sea.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bay' suggests a coastal inlet; it is a bay horse, across whose back a pouch hangs.
explanation.definitionFit: These are pouches hung over a horse's back behind the rider, which is a bay in this clue.

clue.text: Scandalise a missionary by the way one speaks

indicators.note: the way one speaks means the words are heard, not spelt

parts.note: St Paul is the great missionary of the New Testament, so a missionary is a Paul

explanation.surface: A missionary shocks people with his manner of speech.
explanation.definitionFit: To appal is to shock or horrify, much as scandalising does.

clue.text: Spotted cake's unfinished state?

definitions.meaning: a cake not yet topped with icing, read as two words

explanation.definitionFit: Spotted means seen; split into two words it describes a cake lacking icing.

clue.text: Black bird to seek prey

definitions.meaning: a large glossy black crow, or as an adjective a glossy black colour
as a verb, to hunt ravenously for plunder or food

explanation.definitionFit: The noun names a jet-black corvid; the verb, related to ravenous, means to prowl for plunder.

clue.text: Argument after partnership accepts a deal

indicators.note: one piece coming after another sets the argument behind the partnership

parts.note: in cricket a stand is a partnership between two batsmen
a spat is a petty quarrel

explanation.surface: A row breaks out after two business partners agree to a deal.
explanation.walkthrough: A cricket 'stand' is the runs two batsmen put on together, their partnership. 'Partnership' looks like a business arrangement, but it is the cricket sense.
explanation.definitionFit: In poker, to keep one's hand without drawing is to accept the deal as dealt, hence to refuse change.

clue.text: Forcibly push pawn with impatience to attack two men

parts.note: P is the chess notation for a pawn
an itch is a restless longing, impatience to do something
in chess a fork is a move attacking two of the opponent's men at once

explanation.surface: A chess player angrily shoves a pawn forward, eager to threaten two pieces.
explanation.walkthrough: The chess setting makes 'two men' look like people; they are chessmen, and a fork attacks two at once.
explanation.definitionFit: To thrust someone abruptly into a position, as with a hay fork, is to shove them forcibly.

clue.text: Shrub I planted in return visit

indicators.note: something planted in another is set inside it, so the letter goes within
return means the word for visit is read backwards

parts.note: to pay a call is to make a visit

explanation.surface: A gardener puts in a bush on a second trip to the nursery.
explanation.walkthrough: 'return' turns CALL into LLAC; 'planted in' puts I inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: The plant is a flowering bush with scented mauve or white blooms.

clue.text: Meals with last of spare rib

parts.note: teas are light afternoon or evening meals

indicators.note: the last of a word is its final letter, here from spare

explanation.surface: Dinners served with a final helping of spare rib.
explanation.walkthrough: 'spare rib' reads as a cut of pork, but 'rib' is the definition, meaning to make fun of.
explanation.definitionFit: To rib someone is to poke fun at them playfully, a synonym of taunting good-humouredly.

clue.text: Conductor holds baton in chosen direction

indicators.note: in puts the baton inside the other pieces

parts.note: elect means chosen, as in president-elect
E for east is a compass direction
a baton is a rod

explanation.surface: An orchestra leader holds his stick pointing the chosen way.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Conductor' and 'baton' paint an orchestra; the conductor is electrical.
explanation.definitionFit: An electrode is a conductor through which current enters or leaves a cell or circuit.

clue.text: Cut short committee that may support one's paper

parts.note: to clip is to cut short, as with hair or a hedge
a board is a governing committee

explanation.surface: A committee trims a document it may later back.
explanation.definitionFit: It is a stiff writing board with a spring clamp that holds and supports sheets for writing on.

clue.text: Gossip is spread about people in detached homes

indicators.note: the two letters are spread out around the gossip

parts.note: taken as written
slander is malicious gossip

explanation.surface: Rumour circulates about the residents of detached houses.
explanation.walkthrough: 'detached homes' looks like suburban houses; it means homes cut off by water.
explanation.definitionFit: Inhabitants of an isle live in homes set apart by sea from the mainland.

clue.text: Be horrified about nuclear weapon finally dropped in vengeance

indicators.note: its final letter dropped, so the weapon loses its last letter

parts.note: an A-bomb is an atomic, nuclear weapon
Ate is the Greek goddess of ruin and retribution

explanation.surface: Being appalled at an atomic bomb finally being dropped in retaliation.
explanation.walkthrough: 'finally dropped' cuts the B from ABOMB, leaving ABOM; 'dropped' suggests the bombing itself.
explanation.definitionFit: To abominate is to loathe or detest something, regarding it with horror.

clue.text: Page turn in right place is of benefit to chapter

indicators.note: in tells us the turn goes inside the word for right
place instructs us to set the turn into position within the other word

parts.note: right as in a right mess means real or genuine
a bend is a turn in a road or river

explanation.surface: A page is turned at just the right spot in a church document.
explanation.walkthrough: 'right' is the colloquial intensifier, as in 'a right fool', meaning real. A prebend is a canon's share of cathedral income.
explanation.definitionFit: A prebend is the stipend a canon draws from cathedral revenues, so the adjective relates to that benefice of a chapter member.

clue.text: Duck finds edible plant at bottom of river

indicators.note: in a down clue at the bottom of means placed below the other piece

parts.note: the Po is a river in northern Italy
chard is a leafy vegetable

explanation.surface: A duck discovers a vegetable on the riverbed.
explanation.definitionFit: The pochard is a diving duck with a chestnut head.

clue.text: Explain away damage after end of evening

indicators.note: after places the damage behind the evening's last letter
the end of a word is its final letter, here from evening

parts.note: a loss is harm or damage suffered

explanation.surface: An attempt to excuse some harm done late at night.
explanation.definitionFit: To gloss over a fault is to smooth it with a plausible explanation, so it is explained away.

clue.text: Gets excited about some people's portion

indicators.note: about means around, so the jumbled letters surround the people
excited means stirred up, so the letters are jumbled

parts.note: men are some people

explanation.surface: Excitement grips a share of the crowd.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Gets excited' looks like a person's mood; the letters of 'Gets' are the ones stirred up.
explanation.definitionFit: A segment is a piece or section of a whole.

clue.text: Approach time for supernatural omen

parts.note: to come is to approach

explanation.surface: The moment draws near for a ghostly portent to appear.
explanation.definitionFit: A blazing tailed body in the night sky was long read as a portent of disaster.

clue.text: Laughs at exams

definitions.meaning: practice exams taken before the real ones

explanation.definitionFit: The verb means ridicules; the noun names British practice exams sat before the real ones.

clue.text: Very taxing work in gunship

indicators.note: to work something is to manipulate it, so the letters are reshaped

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Serving aboard an armed helicopter is gruelling duty.
explanation.walkthrough: 'work' rearranges IN and GUNSHIP together; 'work' looks like the noun for a job.
explanation.definitionFit: A punishing schedule is gruelling and exhausting, demanding a heavy toll of effort.

clue.text: Give direction to fielder

definitions.meaning: indicate a way with a finger
in cricket, a fielding position close to the batsman on the off side

explanation.definitionFit: To indicate a way is to aim one's finger; in cricket it is also a fielding position square of the batsman.

clue.text: Way to take bad photograph

parts.note: ST is the abbreviation for street, a way
ill means bad, as in ill effects

explanation.surface: A method for taking a poor snapshot.
explanation.walkthrough: 'take' sounds like photography, but it is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A still is a single photograph, especially one from a film.

clue.text: Hermit has an uninteresting job? That's about it

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the dull task goes round the little word

parts.note: a chore is a tedious task
taken as written

explanation.surface: A recluse is asked whether they have a dull occupation, and says that's about the size of it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'That's about it' reads as a weary shrug, but 'about' is the container signal.
explanation.definitionFit: A religious recluse who lives walled up in seclusion is a kind of hermit.

clue.text: Picture that's in publication? On the contrary

indicators.note: in, read with the reversal of roles that follows, sets one piece within the other
on the contrary swaps the roles, so the publication goes inside instead

parts.note: that's means that is, abbreviated i.e.
a mag, short for magazine, is a publication

explanation.surface: A photo appearing in a magazine, or perhaps the other way round.
explanation.walkthrough: 'that's in publication' read literally would put the abbreviation inside the magazine; 'On the contrary' swaps which piece goes inside.
explanation.definitionFit: An image is a picture or likeness.

clue.text: Refusal to accept decline reported

indicators.note: reported means spoken, so the word for decline is heard rather than spelt

parts.note: a descent is a decline or downward slope

explanation.surface: Someone refuses to accept a reported downturn.
explanation.definitionFit: Dissent is disagreement, a refusal to go along with accepted opinion.

clue.text: Pointing out special offer including one good lot of books

indicators.note: including means containing, so the offer wraps around the numeral

parts.note: a sale offers goods at reduced prices
I is the Roman numeral for one
the New Testament, abbreviated NT, is a collection of books of the Good Book

explanation.surface: A bookshop's promotion includes a decent batch of volumes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pointing out' looks like drawing attention; here it means jutting outward.
explanation.definitionFit: A salient angle or line projects outward, as a promontory or a bulge in a battlefront does.
